text:
infra-monitor: :rotating_light: ALERT: multiple ServingRuntime pod restarts for model=redwood-7b-v2 on gpu-node-43 (7 restarts in 5m). Exit summary: CUDA OOM during prefill phase.

cheng (oncall): I'm on it. paging handoff to @maria and @noah. tagging incident-bot to create an incident.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-004 created (sev=page). Participants: cheng (oncall), maria (eng-runtime), noah (sre), emily (support).

maria (eng-runtime): Seen similar pattern earlier but usually for very long context windows. Can someone dump recent logs from the pod?

noah (sre): Pasted from gpu-node-43 /var/log/serving/runtime.log: 
```
2026-03-15T07:12:10Z ERROR runtime: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.2 GiB for prefill kv cache
2026-03-15T07:12:10Z INFO runtime: falling back to container restart (OOM)
2026-03-15T07:12:11Z WARN kubelet: container exited with status 137
2026-03-15T07:12:11Z INFO autoscaler: restart-count=7 backoff=30s
```

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks. This is prefill OOM (token prefix allocation) — long prompt from a customer triggered a large KV allocation. We have two immediate options: 1) reject prefill > N tokens at the router, 2) enable short-circuit fallback (drop prefill KV and stream from smaller cache) per-pod.

cheng (oncall): prioritize mitigation to stop customer impact. How many customers are affected?

emily (support): Looking at error rates and support tickets — 3 customers reporting generation failures around 07:12-07:15 UTC. Two are high-throughput apps (approx 120 reqs/min each) using long-context features. Impact: increased 5xxs and retries, some latency spikes.

noah (sre): Quick mitigation I can apply: mark node-43 as cordoned for new prefill workloads and scale-up dedicated pool by 2 GPUs to absorb load. Running: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-43 && rdctl autoscale --pool=dedicated-gpu --add=2`

maria (eng-runtime): I'm going to push a hotpatch to the runtime to cap prefill allocation at 2048 tokens and enable graceful rejection path (returns 413 with actionable message). Preparing PR and will push canary to the non-prod zone first.

deploy-bot: deploy start: runtime-hotfix/preload-cap-2048 -> canary (zone-east-2).

cheng (oncall): If we can reject long prefill early that's best. But we also need short-term defense: throttling or queuing to avoid repeated retries driving the node into restarts.

noah (sre): Applied cordon. Also patched the router to add a temporary rule: `if request.prefill_length > 2450 -> 429 with Retry-After: 10`. Pushing now.

maria (eng-runtime): Canary applied. Observing canary logs: prefill allocation attempts >2048 are now being rejected with clear message. No crash on canary.

cheng (oncall): Emily — please prepare a short customer notification for the three impacted accounts explaining we saw prefill OOMs for very long prompts and we've put temporary limits; provide ETA for follow-up.

emily (support): Drafting: "We detected resource errors caused by very large context requests; we've implemented a temporary limit on prefills > ~2k tokens to prevent instability. This is temporary while we roll runtime fixes; ETA for full resolution: 4-8 hours. If you need a higher limit for an agreed SLA we can coordinate a dedicated capacity plan." Will post to the two affected customers and CSMs in 10m.

noah (sre): Monitoring cluster: restart rate on gpu-node-43 has dropped from 7 in 5m to 0 in the last 6m after cordon + router rule. Error rate for redwood-7b-v2 from affected AZ down 85%.

maria (eng-runtime): Next steps: 1) merge hotfix and roll to production (30m rollout), 2) add safer KV allocation (sparsified prefill) in next minor release, 3) add metric and alert for prefills > token_threshold. Filing follow-up ticket: RUNTIME-1563.

cheng (oncall): Sounds good. I'm keeping the incident open until the hotfix is live and customer comms are sent. Incident-bot: update status to "mitigated - in progress".

incident-bot: INC-2026-004 status updated to mitigated:in_progress.

maria (eng-runtime): Hotfix merged and rolling to prod. Rolling window: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 20m with health checks (reject >2048 at router remains until full rollout completes).

deploy-bot: deploy success: runtime-hotfix/preload-cap-2048 -> prod (100%).

noah (sre): Observability: 5xxs back to baseline, no further restarts on gpu-node-43 for 40m. Marking node for uncordon after we confirm steady state for 1h.

emily (support): Customer messages sent. Two customers acknowledged, one requested dedicated capacity; routed to sales/CS.

cheng (oncall): Closing plan: keep alert thresholds tight for next 24h, add prefill token histogram to dashboard, and follow-up RUNTIME-1563 for allocation improvement. I'll close incident once dashboard shows stable for 60m.

maria (eng-runtime): Quick note for postmortem: include sample offending prompt (sanitized), the exact KV allocation size when crash happened, and why the prior guardrails didn't trip.

noah (sre): I'll create the postmortem doc and tag owners.

cheng (oncall): :thumbsup: Great work everyone — nice fast mitigation.

(End of thread)
